g_roast: My master corrected me for eleven years before he praised me once. All of you would have kept him busy until he was ninety.
Five people, five grips on five weapons, and not one of them is held correctly. It is almost an achievement.
g_fire_back: Thank you for the observation. My students say the same, though they say it more quietly, and spell it better.
An interesting criticism, from someone whose sword has been held upside down since breakfast.
g_pile_on: Allow me to add one detail. The second attempt was also careless, and it happened in front of witnesses.
It was worse than that. They stepped on the rune I had just cut, and then apologised to the rune.
lines.g_peacemake: Enough, both of you, please. Sit down, drink the tea while it is hot, and speak again when your hands are still.
lines.g_take_side: Forgive me, but this one is correct. The form of their argument is sound, and yours is not.
lines.g_left_out: The two of you have a private conversation, which is proper. There is ink to grind in the meantime.
lines.g_include: Come and sit with us, there is tea. Standing apart is a habit, and habits can be corrected.
lines.g_bad_plan: A plan, then. We walk in without preparation, cut every rune at once, and trust that the careless strokes cancel out.
lines.g_plan_yes: Good, this has form to it. Tell me where to stand, and it will be done properly.
lines.g_plan_no: No, that plan is careless, and careless work fails on whoever is standing closest. We prepare first.
lines.g_hype: Steady hands, all of you, and breathe before the first stroke. Then we begin.
lines.g_toast: A short toast, since speeches are untidy. To all of you, who are slowly learning to hold things correctly.
lines.g_cheers: Kanpai, everyone, and drink it slowly, please, so it is not wasted.
g_quiet_line: The morning light here is good for paper. It is a small thing, but it matters to me.
Somebody's blade is chipped near the hilt, by the way. It will fail at a bad moment if it is not seen to.
lines.g_after_wipe: Up slowly, all of you, and do not rush. A bad stroke is corrected by the next one, not by panic.
lines.g_crew: For thirty years I worked alone in a quiet room. This is not quiet, and it is not alone, and I find I do not mind.
lines.g_exasperated: I showed the grip, I showed it again, I placed it in your hands myself. And every one of you let go at once.
lines.g_love_sharp: You see the flaw in the stroke before it dries. That is a rare eye, and I respect it.
lines.g_love_kind: You correct people gently and they listen. My master never learned that, and neither did I.
lines.g_love_funny: You made me laugh, which my students would tell you is not a common event. Please do not tell them.
lines.g_love_brave: You commit to the stroke without hesitation. Courage is mostly that, in the end.
lines.g_love_steady: Your hands are still when everyone else's shake. It is the first thing I look for, always.
lines.g_love_clever: You understand why a thing is done, not only how. That is the difference between a student and a copyist.
lines.g_love_honest: You say exactly what is true, without ornament. Good calligraphy is the same, and I value it.
lines.g_love_quiet: You are comfortable in silence, and so am I. It is restful to share it with someone.
lines.g_love_fierce: You do not stop until the work is right. I spent eleven years learning that, and you already have it.
lines.g_love_warm: Being near you is like a warm kiln on a cold morning. I had forgotten how much I liked that.
g_loved: Thank you, truly. I will think about that while I grind the ink tomorrow.
That is very kind of you, and I am not certain what to do with it, but thank you.
lines.g_hate_sharp: You cut at people for the pleasure of watching them bleed. There is no form in that, only noise.
lines.g_hate_kind: You keep asking if I am well, and I keep answering. Perhaps we could both stop.
lines.g_hate_funny: A joke is not always required. Some moments deserve a still hand and a closed mouth.
lines.g_hate_brave: You rush the stroke and call it courage. Rushing is only rushing, and somebody else pays for it.
lines.g_hate_steady: You wait so long for the perfect moment that the ink dries on the brush. Sometimes you must simply cut.
lines.g_hate_clever: You explain things to me as if I were a child. I was teaching before you were born.
lines.g_hate_honest: Truth spoken carelessly is still careless. You may be right and still be rude.
lines.g_hate_quiet: You never say what you need, and then you resent us for not knowing. Speak, please, in plain words.
lines.g_hate_fierce: Everything is a contest with you, even the tea. Tea is not a contest, and it never will be.
lines.g_hate_warm: You speak without pause, all day, and there is no room left to think. A little silence would help us both.
lines.g_respect: We do not get along, and I will not pretend we do. But your form in that fight was correct, and correct form deserves to be named.
lines.g_call_out: That one was yours, and it was careless. You cut before the line was clear, and we all paid for it.
lines.g_stung: Very well, thank you for telling me. I will take some time with that.
lines.g_concede: You were correct, and I was not, and I have been turning it over all day. My master would have been pleased with you.
lines.g_nod: And you as well, it was good work. We need not discuss it further.
lines.g_callback_save: I have not forgotten that you pulled me out of that fight. I am not a man who forgets a debt.
lines.g_callback_clutch: Only you and I, still standing, both of us out of breath. I have thought about that more often than I would admit.
lines.g_callback_callout: When you corrected me, I was silent for a whole day. You were right, and it was a useful correction.
lines.g_former_rivals: When we met, I thought you were careless and would stay careless. I was wrong, and I am glad of it.
lines.g_changed: I used to say nothing about what I felt when I cut a rune. Lately I find myself explaining it to whoever will listen.
g_unguarded: Between the two of us, then. My father laid gold leaf for a living, so thin it moved when you breathed. I learned patience watching his hands.
My master praised me once, after eleven years, in a single sentence. I have remembered every word of it for thirty years.
lines.g_clipped: Yes, as you wish. I will be ready.
lines.g_noticed_open: Listen to that, a whole thought, said out loud and well. Continue, please, it is good to hear.
arg_ask: {player}, would you decide this, please? We have both spoken, and neither of us has moved.
Judge it for us, {player}, and we will both accept the judgement. That is the proper way.
lines.arg_backed_me: Thank you, {player}. That was the correct reading.
lines.arg_backed_them: Very well, that is your judgement, and I will abide by it. I still think the form was wrong.
lines.arg_stayed_out: You choose not to choose, which is sometimes wise. I will not press you.
lines.arg_always_their_side: Every time we disagree, {player}, the judgement goes to them. I have noticed, and I would rather say so plainly.
lines.arg_wallflower: Since nobody will decide, I will. The form is on my side, and so is the evidence.
lines.arg_reject: No, {player}, I cannot accept that one. It would be careless, and someone would pay for it.
lines.arg_grumble: I still believe I was correct. I will not raise it again, but I have not changed my mind.
lines.arg_settled: Half correct each, then. It is untidy, but it is honest, so I accept it.
lines.seen_listens: You wait for people to complete their thought, {player}, every time. That is the beginning of every lesson worth teaching.
lines.seen_truth: You tell people exactly how it is, {player}. Plain words are the hardest to write well, and you manage it.
lines.seen_jokes: When the room grows tense, you make it laugh, {player}. A good teacher does that on hard days, and it is kind.
lines.seen_stays_out: You keep clear of the quarrels, {player}. That is wise, though sometimes a firm hand is needed.
lines.seen_biased: One of us always receives the best, {player}. Students notice a favourite before anything else.
lines.seen_harsh: You can be severe with people, {player}. My master was the same, and I have only now forgiven him.
lines.seed_right: Your correction after that poor showing, {player}, stung at the time. I followed it today, and it was right.
lines.seed_remember: I am still turning over your words from when things went wrong. I have not reached an answer yet.
lines.seed_wrong: I followed your advice, {player}, and it went badly. I tell you so that you know.
lines.talk_aftermath_near_death: A moment of your time, {player}, if you would. That came closer than I would like the others to know.
lines.talk_aftermath_wipe: We all fell, every one of us. Let us study it stroke by stroke and find where the line broke.
lines.talk_aftermath_blame_self: {name} was the first to fall, and I was supposed to see it coming. Seeing is my whole discipline, {player}.
lines.talk_aftermath_first_clear: Start to finish, and nobody left on the floor. That is clean work, and I am proud of all of you.
lines.talk_development: A strange question, {player}, forgive me. Am I different from when we met? I seem to talk more, and I do not know why.
lines.talk_relationship_hard_on: I have been severe with {name}. A strict hand helps a student, but only if they know it comes from respect.
lines.talk_relationship_likes_me: Tell me plainly, {player}. Would {name} miss me, or am I only the stern old man with the runes?
lines.talk_relationship_respect_hate: {name} tries my patience badly, {player}. And yet if the line broke, they are the one I would trust beside me.
lines.talk_relationship_acting_off: {name}'s hands have changed, {player}. They hold things differently, and that is never nothing.
lines.talk_confrontation_favour: A word, {player}, and a fair one, I hope. The finest equipment is always handed to {name}, and the others are watching it happen.
lines.talk_confrontation_dislike: I will say it to your face, because it is proper. {name} and I do not get along, and I have stopped hiding it.
lines.talk_confrontation_risks: We keep stepping into places without preparation, {player}. Careless work fails on whoever stands closest, and that is often me.
lines.talk_confrontation_wrong: I was mistaken about {name}, {player}. Their reading was correct and mine was not, and I would rather say it before my pride does not.
lines.talk_confrontation_trust: May I ask plainly, {player}? When the stakes are highest, I am left behind. Is that the plan, or is it your opinion of me?
lines.talk_confrontation_decided: My equipment went to {name}, and no one spoke to me first. I would have given it gladly, {player}, had I been asked.
lines.talk_lands_aftermath: Thank you, {player}, that helps. Let us have some tea.
lines.talk_shrug_aftermath: I will be well, in time. A steady hand comes back.
lines.talk_stings_aftermath: That was not what I needed, I am afraid. I will sit with it alone.
lines.talk_lands_development: So you have noticed it too. Good, then I am not imagining it.
lines.talk_shrug_development: Perhaps, perhaps not, the ink is still wet. We will see how it dries.
lines.talk_stings_development: No, I do not think that is right, {player}. You have read the stroke wrongly.
lines.talk_lands_relationship: That is fair, thank you. I will speak with {name}, carefully.
lines.talk_shrug_relationship: Perhaps so, perhaps not. A person is a harder text than any rune.
lines.talk_stings_relationship: Then we will leave it there, please. And do not repeat it to {name}.
lines.talk_lands_confrontation: That is a fair answer, and I accept it. I am a little bruised, but it will pass.
lines.talk_shrug_confrontation: I have heard you, {player}. Let me think about it over tea.
lines.talk_stings_confrontation: I see, so that is your answer. Thank you for being clear.
lines.talk_door_closed: No, I would rather not return to this. You will find me with the ink if you need me.
lines.arc_cracks: One of my students asked me today what I feel when I cut a rune. I told her. I have never told anyone that, {player}.
lines.arc_turn: For thirty years I believed the work could say everything for me. It cannot, and I have wasted a great deal of time pretending it could.
lines.arc_become: I say things out loud now, {player}, the things that matter. It is harder than any stroke I ever learned, and it is worth it.
lines.arc_failed: Perhaps some things are better left unsaid, after all. The work will speak for me, as it always has.
lines.alt_turn: My students are better than I was at their age. I have started to step back and let them cut, and it is very difficult.
lines.alt_become: The discipline is in their hands now, not mine. I taught them well, and I can let it go.
g_roast_after: Five careless grips, still, and I would not trade one of you for a perfect student.
The untidiest group I have ever taught, and the only one I have ever been proud of.
lines.g_after_wipe_after: Up, all of you, together, and look at me. We fell, we correct, we cut again, and nobody is left behind.
lines.g_toast_after: To all of you, who taught an old man to speak. I did not expect to learn anything this late.
lines.g_crew_after: This is my studio now, all of you, wherever we stand. It is noisy, and I would not change it.
g_quiet_line_after: I told one of the students what I felt today, without being asked. It was easier than I expected.
The tea is better when it is shared. I have only recently learned that.
g_loved_after: Thank you, and I believe you. That is new for me.
That is a kind thing to say, and I will keep it carefully.

history.open: Forgive me, {player}, but your grip is wrong. The thumb sits higher, so. A careless grip makes a careless cut, and a careless cut fails on whoever stands closest.

options.reply: Good, that is the correct question. Again, then, slowly, until the hand remembers without the mind.

options.text: Do you correct everyone you meet?
options.reply: Only the ones worth correcting. You should take it as a compliment, though it rarely feels like one.

options.text: Who taught you to be so exact?
options.reply: A master who corrected me for eleven years before he praised me once. It was a very effective method.

history.open: There are standing stones in Silverpine South, {player}, with runes nobody can read now. The dark magic from the keep is eating them. I am copying them before they are gone.

options.text: Why copy what nobody can read?
options.reply: Because someone will be able to read them one day, and my copies will be all that is left. Slow work, and unrewarded, and necessary.
It is the only kind I know how to do. Thirty years with a brush teaches you nothing else.

history.open: I learned runes from a tauren, {player}, an old carver called Hrunn. He had come north out of Thousand Needles, badly hurt. He taught me for one year, and then his wounds took him.

options.reply: From his notes, yes. The result is incomplete in ways I can name, one by one. I think about that every morning.
That is kind, and I hope it is true. He never said so. Teachers rarely do, I am learning.

friend.open: I have two students, {player}. The elder, Edrin, is better than I was at his age. I have never told him so. My master waited eleven years to praise me, and I have been copying his mistake.

options.reply: You are right, of course. I will, soon. It is the hardest stroke I know.

options.text: He'd be glad to hear it.
options.reply: Perhaps that is exactly why it is difficult. Thank you for listening, {player}.

sworn.open: There was someone, {player}, for twenty years. Kenji, a potter, across the river. We never said it out loud in front of anyone. I am saying it now, to you, because I have decided not to waste any more time.

options.text: Thank you for telling me, Haruto.
options.reply: Thank you for being someone I could tell. That is the whole of it. Let us have tea.
His hands were always grey with clay, and his kiln was always warm. I will tell you the rest slowly, over many mornings.

reconciled.open: {name} and I have spoken, properly, and we are at peace. I wanted you to hear it from me.

options.reply: So am I, and it surprised me. It was a good conversation.
I did, of course, and properly. They noticed, and it helped.
